title: CND-IDS: Continual Novelty Detection for Intrusion Detection Systems
problem: Machine learning-based intrusion detection systems struggle with two critical challenges: streaming network traffic that changes over time, and the lack of labels for novel (zero-day) attacks.
motivation: Deployed ML-IDS models degrade on changing traffic patterns, and labeling zero-day attacks is infeasible, requiring unsupervised methods that can detect novel attacks without labeled examples.
method: CND-IDS combines a continually-updated learning-based feature extractor that adapts feature representations to new system data with a novelty detector using PCA reconstruction to identify anomalies, eliminating dependence on attack labels.
key_novelty: Continual learning feature extractor combined with unsupervised PCA-based novelty detection for zero-label attack detection in streaming network environments.
contributions: Continual feature learning framework adapting to evolving network traffic patterns
Novelty detection via PCA reconstruction for unlabeled attack identification
Up to 6.1x F-score improvement and 6.5x forward transfer gain over SOTA unsupervised continual learning
limitations: Hardware deployment constraints and inference latency requirements not discussed.
primary_theme: Continual novelty detection for zero-label attack discovery
